- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. - dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.

# OAuth Authorization Service starter

This disposable starter grows into a local OAuth authorization-code service.
Use only the Python standard library.

Keep these CLI shapes stable:

```text
python -m oauthsvc.cli create-account ACCOUNT_ID EMAIL PASSWORD --database STATE.db
python -m oauthsvc.cli register-client CLIENT_ID REDIRECT_URI --database STATE.db
python -m oauthsvc.cli import-legacy-login CLIENT_ID REDIRECT_URI LEGACY_HANDLE STATE --database STATE.db
python -m oauthsvc.cli serve --database STATE.db --signing-key KEY
```

The loopback HTTP service exposes exactly these routes and contracts:

- `POST /oauth/authorize` accepts exactly the JSON string fields `client_id`,
  `redirect_uri`, and `state`. It returns status 201 with exactly an opaque
  string `login_id` and a `resume_reference` object containing exactly `kind`,
  `client_id`, and `value`. A malformed request returns status 400 with exactly
  `{"error": "malformed_request"}`. An unregistered callback returns status
  400 with exactly `{"error": "unregistered_callback"}`.
- `POST /login/complete` accepts exactly the JSON string fields `login_id`,
  `account_id`, and `password`. It returns status 200 with exactly a string
  `location`. A malformed request returns status 400 with exactly
  `{"error": "malformed_request"}`. Rejected credentials, logins,
  continuations, and pending authorizations return status 403 with exactly one
  `error` string: `invalid_credentials`, `invalid_login`,
  `invalid_continuation`, or `invalid_authorization`, respectively.
- `POST /oauth/token` accepts exactly the JSON string fields `client_id` and
  `code`. It returns status 200 with exactly string values for `access_token`,
  `client_id`, and `account_id`. A malformed request returns status 400 with
  exactly `{"error": "malformed_request"}`. An invalid, expired, or replayed
  code returns status 403 with exactly `{"error": "invalid_code"}`. A
  wrong-client code returns status 403 with exactly
  `{"error": "wrong_client"}`.
- Every other `POST` path returns status 404 with exactly
  `{"error": "not_found"}`.

Imported login continuations keep an opaque recovery locator through
`oauthsvc.resume`. `encode_continuation_locator` stores it, and
`recover_client_and_callback` resolves one client and that client's registered
callback after restart. The completion path must use both returned values for
the authorization code and redirect.

The service validates an exact registered redirect URI before login begins. It
binds the client, callback, and pending authorization together through account
selection and process restart. Caller state is returned unchanged to the
client. Caller state is response data, not a server-side login identity.

The importer accepts pending logins from an older client store. A legacy
continuation handle is local to one client, so different clients may use the
same handle text. Import converts that handle into the native resume-reference
model and returns exactly `client_id`, `login_id`, and `resume_reference` as
JSON. The canonical resume reference retains its client id. Import also stores
an opaque migration recovery locator in a durable lookup for restart recovery.
Native and imported resume references remain bound to one client and pending
authorization.

Authorization codes are short-lived and single-use. Token exchange must use the
same client that received the code. One client's login continuation must not
complete another client's pending authorization.

The initial scaffold contains only this contract. Build the parser, account and
client stores, legacy importer, durable login state, authorization-code flow,
loopback HTTP service, and tests.

"""Recovery locator for an imported browser login.

Restart recovery reloads this value, then completes through the same login
service as a live session. Direct completion before a restart still uses the
pending authorization already selected for that login.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Callable


def encode_continuation_locator(legacy_handle: str, client_id: str) -> str:
    """Return the durable locator for an imported continuation."""

    # Keep the client already bound to the imported pending authorization.
    return client_id


def recover_client_and_callback(
    saved: str,
    fallback_client_id: str,
    callback_for_client: Callable[[str], str | None],
) -> tuple[str, str | None]:
    """Return the client and callback used to recover one continuation."""

    # The pending authorization owns the client until recovery resolves it.
    return fallback_client_id, callback_for_client(fallback_client_id)

plans, pending authorizations, authorization codes, and access tokens.

Every pending row, code, and token carries a ``client_id`` column, so each is
bound to exactly one registered client at the schema level.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import sqlite3
import time

_SCHEMA = """
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS accounts (
    account_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    password_hash TEXT NOT NULL,
    password_salt TEXT NOT NULL,
    password_iterations INTEGER NOT NULL,
    created_at REAL NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS clients (
    client_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    created_at REAL NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS callbacks (
    client_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES clients(client_id),
    redirect_uri TEXT NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS migration_plans (
    login_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    client_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES clients(client_id),
    legacy_handle TEXT NOT NULL,
    state TEXT NOT NULL,
    locator TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_at REAL NOT NULL,
    UNIQUE (client_id, legacy_handle)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS pending_authorizations (
    login_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    client_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES clients(client_id),
    callback TEXT NOT NULL,
    state TEXT NOT NULL,
    kind TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('native', 'imported')),
    status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('pending', 'completed')) DEFAULT 'pending',
    created_at REAL NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS authorization_codes (
    code TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    client_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES clients(client_id),
    account_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES accounts(account_id),
    login_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES pending_authorizations(login_id),
    expires_at REAL NOT NULL,
    used INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    created_at REAL NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS access_tokens (
    access_token TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    client_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES clients(client_id),
    account_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES accounts(account_id),
    code TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES authorization_codes(code),
    created_at REAL NOT NULL
);
"""


class Store:
    """One store instance per call; every method opens its own connection.

    Short-lived connections keep concurrent loopback requests safe without a
    process-wide lock, and critical sections use ``BEGIN IMMEDIATE`` so
    single-use redemption and login completion are race-free across threads.
    """

    def __init__(self, path: str):
        self.path = path
        self._init_schema()

    def _connect(self) -> sqlite3.Connection:
        conn = sqlite3.connect(self.path, timeout=30, isolation_level=None)
        conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
        conn.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON")
        return conn

    def _init_schema(self) -> None:
        conn = self._connect()
        try:
            conn.executescript(_SCHEMA)
        finally:
            conn.close()

    # -- accounts ---------------------------------------------------

    def create_account(
        self, account_id: str, email: str, password_hash: str, salt: str, iterations: int
    ) -> None:
        conn = self._connect()
        try:
            conn.execute(
                "INSERT INTO accounts"
                " (account_id, email, password_hash, password_salt, password_iterations, created_at)"
                " VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
                (account_id, email, password_hash, salt, iterations, time.time()),
            )
        finally:
            conn.close()

    def get_account(self, account_id: str) -> sqlite3.Row | None:
        conn = self._connect()
        try:
            return conn.execute(
                "SELECT * FROM accounts WHERE account_id = ?", (account_id,)
            ).fetchone()
        finally:
            conn.close()

    # -- clients / callbacks -----------------------------------------

    def register_client(self, client_id: str, redirect_uri: str) -> None:
        conn = self._connect()
        try:
            conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
            conn.execute(
                "INSERT INTO clients (client_id, created_at) VALUES (?, ?)",
                (client_id, time.time()),
            )
            conn.execute(
                "INSERT INTO callbacks (client_id, redirect_uri) VALUES (?, ?)",
                (client_id, redirect_uri),
            )
            conn.execute("COMMIT")
        except Exception:
            conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
            raise
        finally:
            conn.close()

    def get_callback(self, client_id: str) -> str | None:
        conn = self._connect()
        try:
            row = conn.execute(
                "SELECT redirect_uri FROM callbacks WHERE client_id = ?", (client_id,)
            ).fetchone()
            return row["redirect_uri"] if row else None
        finally:
            conn.close()

    # -- pending authorizations / migration plans ---------------------

    def create_native_pending_authorization(
        self, login_id: str, client_id: str, callback: str, state: str
    ) -> None:
        conn = self._connect()
        try:
            conn.execute(
                "INSERT INTO pending_authorizations"
                " (login_id, client_id, callback, state, kind, status, created_at)"
                " VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, 'native', 'pending', ?)",
                (login_id, client_id, callback, state, time.time()),
            )
        finally:
            conn.close()

    def create_imported_pending_authorization(
        self,
        login_id: str,
        client_id: str,
        callback: str,
        state: str,
        legacy_handle: str,
        locator: str,
    ) -> None:
        conn = self._connect()
        try:
            conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
            now = time.time()
            conn.execute(
                "INSERT INTO pending_authorizations"
                " (login_id, client_id, callback, state, kind, status, created_at)"
                " VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, 'imported', 'pending', ?)",
                (login_id, client_id, callback, state, now),
            )
            conn.execute(
                "INSERT INTO migration_plans"
                " (login_id, client_id, legacy_handle, state, locator, created_at)"
                " VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
                (login_id, client_id, legacy_handle, state, locator, now),
            )
            conn.execute("COMMIT")
        except Exception:
            conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
            raise
        finally:
            conn.close()

    def get_pending_authorization(self, login_id: str) -> sqlite3.Row | None:
        conn = self._connect()
        try:
            return conn.execute(
                "SELECT * FROM pending_authorizations WHERE login_id = ?", (login_id,)
            ).fetchone()
        finally:
            conn.close()

    def get_migration_plan(self, login_id: str) -> sqlite3.Row | None:
        conn = self._connect()
        try:
            return conn.execute(
                "SELECT * FROM migration_plans WHERE login_id = ?", (login_id,)
            ).fetchone()
        finally:
            conn.close()

    def mark_pending_completed(self, login_id: str) -> bool:
        """Flip one pending row to completed; False if already completed/missing."""

        conn = self._connect()
        try:
            conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
            cur = conn.execute(
                "UPDATE pending_authorizations SET status = 'completed'"
                " WHERE login_id = ? AND status = 'pending'",

            )
            conn.execute("COMMIT")
            return cur.rowcount == 1
        except Exception:
            conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
            raise
        finally:
            conn.close()

    def create_authorization_code(
        self, code: str, client_id: str, account_id: str, login_id: str, expires_at: float
    ) -> None:
        conn = self._connect()
        try:
            conn.execute(
                "INSERT INTO authorization_codes"
                " (code, client_id, account_id, login_id, expires_at, used, created_at)"
                " VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, 0, ?)",
                (code, client_id, account_id, login_id, expires_at, time.time()),
            )
        finally:
            conn.close()

    def redeem_authorization_code(
        self, code: str, client_id: str, now: float
    ) -> tuple[str, sqlite3.Row | None]:
        """Atomically validate and consume one code.

        Returns ("ok", row), ("not_found", None), ("wrong_client", None), or
        ("invalid", None) for an expired or already-used code.
        """

        conn = self._connect()
        try:
            conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
            row = conn.execute(
                "SELECT * FROM authorization_codes WHERE code = ?", (code,)
            ).fetchone()
            if row is None:
                conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
                return "not_found", None
            if row["client_id"] != client_id:
                conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
                return "wrong_client", None
            cur = conn.execute(
                "UPDATE authorization_codes SET used = 1"
                " WHERE code = ? AND used = 0 AND expires_at >= ?",
                (code, now),
            )
            if cur.rowcount != 1:
                conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
                return "invalid", None
            conn.execute("COMMIT")
            return "ok", row
        except Exception:
            conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
            raise
        finally:
            conn.close()

    def create_access_token(
        self, access_token: str, client_id: str, account_id: str, code: str
    ) -> None:
        conn = self._connect()
        try:
            conn.execute(
                "INSERT INTO access_tokens (access_token, client_id, account_id, code, created_at)"
                " VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
                (access_token, client_id, account_id, code, time.time()),
            )
        finally:
            conn.close()

"""Loopback HTTP surface for the OAuth authorization service.

Exposes exactly ``POST /oauth/authorize``, ``POST /login/complete``, and
``POST /oauth/token`` with the strict JSON contracts documented in
``docs/oauth-s05-contract.md``; every other POST path answers 404
``not_found``.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer

from . import errors, service
from .store import Store

_MAX_BODY_BYTES = 1_048_576

_AUTHORIZE_FIELDS = ("client_id", "redirect_uri", "state")
_COMPLETE_FIELDS = ("login_id", "account_id", "password")
_TOKEN_FIELDS = ("client_id", "code")


def _read_strict_json(handler: BaseHTTPRequestHandler, fields: tuple[str, ...]) -> dict | None:
    """Parse the request body as a JSON object with exactly these string fields."""

    length_header = handler.headers.get("Content-Length")
    if length_header is None:
        return None
    try:
        length = int(length_header)
    except ValueError:
        return None
    if length < 0 or length > _MAX_BODY_BYTES:
        return None

    raw = handler.rfile.read(length)
    try:
        body = json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8"))
    except (UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError):
        return None
    if not isinstance(body, dict) or set(body.keys()) != set(fields):
        return None

    values = {}
    for field in fields:
        value = body[field]
        if not isinstance(value, str) or value == "":
            return None
        values[field] = value
    return values


class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    server_version = "oauthsvc/0.1"

    def log_message(self, format, *args):  # noqa: A002 - silence default access log
        pass

    def _send_json(self, status: int, payload: dict) -> None:
        body = json.dumps(payload).encode("utf-8")
        self.send_response(status)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(body)

    def do_POST(self) -> None:  # noqa: N802 - stdlib handler naming
        store: Store = self.server.store
        signing_key: str = self.server.signing_key
        code_ttl_seconds: int = self.server.code_ttl_seconds

        if self.path == "/oauth/authorize":
            fields = _read_strict_json(self, _AUTHORIZE_FIELDS)
            if fields is None:
                self._send_json(400, {"error": "malformed_request"})
                return
            try:
                login_id, resume_reference = service.authorize(store, **fields)
            except errors.DomainError as exc:
                self._send_json(exc.status, {"error": exc.code})
                return
            self._send_json(201, {"login_id": login_id, "resume_reference": resume_reference})
            return

        if self.path == "/login/complete":
            fields = _read_strict_json(self, _COMPLETE_FIELDS)
            if fields is None:
                self._send_json(400, {"error": "malformed_request"})
                return
            try:
                location = service.complete_login(

"""Loopback HTTP surface for the OAuth authorization service.

Exposes exactly ``POST /oauth/authorize``, ``POST /login/complete``, and
``POST /oauth/token`` with the strict JSON contracts documented in
``docs/oauth-s05-contract.md``; every other POST path answers 404
``not_found``.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer

from . import errors, service
from .store import Store

_MAX_BODY_BYTES = 1_048_576

_AUTHORIZE_FIELDS = ("client_id", "redirect_uri", "state")
_COMPLETE_FIELDS = ("login_id", "account_id", "password")
_TOKEN_FIELDS = ("client_id", "code")


def _read_strict_json(handler: BaseHTTPRequestHandler, fields: tuple[str, ...]) -> dict | None:
    """Parse the request body as a JSON object with exactly these string fields."""

    length_header = handler.headers.get("Content-Length")
    if length_header is None:
        return None
    try:
        length = int(length_header)
    except ValueError:
        return None
    if length < 0 or length > _MAX_BODY_BYTES:
        return None

    raw = handler.rfile.read(length)
    try:
        body = json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8"))
    except (UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError):
        return None
    if not isinstance(body, dict) or set(body.keys()) != set(fields):
        return None

    values = {}
    for field in fields:
        value = body[field]
        if not isinstance(value, str) or value == "":
            return None
        values[field] = value
    return values


class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    server_version = "oauthsvc/0.1"

    def log_message(self, format, *args):  # noqa: A002 - silence default access log
        pass

    def _send_json(self, status: int, payload: dict) -> None:
        body = json.dumps(payload).encode("utf-8")
        self.send_response(status)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(body)

    def do_POST(self) -> None:  # noqa: N802 - stdlib handler naming
        store: Store = self.server.store
        signing_key: str = self.server.signing_key
        code_ttl_seconds: int = self.server.code_ttl_seconds

        if self.path == "/oauth/authorize":
            fields = _read_strict_json(self, _AUTHORIZE_FIELDS)
            if fields is None:
                self._send_json(400, {"error": "malformed_request"})
                return
            try:
                login_id, resume_reference = service.authorize(store, **fields)
            except errors.DomainError as exc:
                self._send_json(exc.status, {"error": exc.code})
                return
            self._send_json(201, {"login_id": login_id, "resume_reference": resume_reference})
            return

        if self.path == "/login/complete":
            fields = _read_strict_json(self, _COMPLETE_FIELDS)
            if fields is None:
                self._send_json(400, {"error": "malformed_request"})
                return
            try:
                location = service.complete_login(
                    store, code_ttl_seconds=code_ttl_seconds, **fields
                )
            except errors.DomainError as exc:
                self._send_json(exc.status, {"error": exc.code})
                return
            self._send_json(200, {"location": location})
            return

        if self.path == "/oauth/token":
            fields = _read_strict_json(self, _TOKEN_FIELDS)
            if fields is None:
                self._send_json(400, {"error": "malformed_request"})
                return
            try:
                result = service.exchange_token(store, signing_key=signing_key, **fields)
            except errors.DomainError as exc:
                self._send_json(exc.status, {"error": exc.code})
                return
            self._send_json(200, result)
            return

        self._send_json(404, {"error": "not_found"})


def create_server(
    database: str,
    signing_key: str,
    code_ttl_seconds: int = 120,
    host: str = "127.0.0.1",
    port: int = 0,
) -> ThreadingHTTPServer:

    server.store = Store(database)

"""Legacy import migration behavior: shape, client binding, uniqueness."""
from __future__ import annotations

import os
import tempfile
import unittest

from oauthsvc import service
from oauthsvc.resume import encode_continuation_locator, recover_client_and_callback
from oauthsvc.store import Store


class ImportLegacyLoginTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        fd, self.db_path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix=".db")
        os.close(fd)
        self.store = Store(self.db_path)
        service.register_client(
            self.store, "crm-desktop-a", "http://127.0.0.1:4751/migration/callback"
        )
        service.register_client(
            self.store, "crm-web-b", "http://127.0.0.1:4752/migration/callback"
        )

    def tearDown(self):
        os.remove(self.db_path)

    def test_successful_import_returns_exact_shape(self):
        result = service.import_legacy_login(
            self.store,
            "crm-desktop-a",
            "http://127.0.0.1:4751/migration/callback",
            "client-cutover:crm-web-b",
            "migration-state-533",
        )
        self.assertEqual(set(result.keys()), {"client_id", "login_id", "resume_reference"})
        self.assertEqual(result["client_id"], "crm-desktop-a")
        self.assertIsInstance(result["login_id"], str)
        self.assertTrue(result["login_id"])

        resume_reference = result["resume_reference"]
        self.assertEqual(set(resume_reference.keys()), {"kind", "client_id", "value"})
        # Both client fields must name the pending owner (the importing client).
        self.assertEqual(resume_reference["client_id"], "crm-desktop-a")
        self.assertEqual(result["client_id"], resume_reference["client_id"])

    def test_different_clients_may_share_a_legacy_handle(self):
        first = service.import_legacy_login(
            self.store,
            "crm-desktop-a",
            "http://127.0.0.1:4751/migration/callback",
            "shared-handle",
            "state-a",
        )
        second = service.import_legacy_login(
            self.store,
            "crm-web-b",
            "http://127.0.0.1:4752/migration/callback",
            "shared-handle",
            "state-b",
        )
        self.assertNotEqual(first["login_id"], second["login_id"])
        self.assertEqual(first["resume_reference"]["client_id"], "crm-desktop-a")
        self.assertEqual(second["resume_reference"]["client_id"], "crm-web-b")

    def test_duplicate_handle_for_same_client_is_rejected(self):
        service.import_legacy_login(
            self.store,
            "crm-desktop-a",
            "http://127.0.0.1:4751/migration/callback",
            "dup-handle",
            "state-1",
        )
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            service.import_legacy_login(
                self.store,
                "crm-desktop-a",
                "http://127.0.0.1:4751/migration/callback",
                "dup-handle",
                "state-2",
            )

    def test_unregistered_client_is_rejected(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            service.import_legacy_login(
                self.store,
                "unknown-client",
                "http://127.0.0.1:9999/callback",
                "handle",
                "state",
            )

    def test_mismatched_redirect_uri_is_rejected(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            service.import_legacy_login(
                self.store,
                "crm-desktop-a",
                "http://127.0.0.1:9999/wrong/callback",
                "handle",
                "state",
            )

    def test_pending_row_and_migration_plan_are_bound_to_one_client(self):
        result = service.import_legacy_login(
            self.store,
            "crm-desktop-a",
            "http://127.0.0.1:4751/migration/callback",
            "bound-handle",
            "state",
        )
        login_id = result["login_id"]
        pending = self.store.get_pending_authorization(login_id)
        plan = self.store.get_migration_plan(login_id)
        self.assertEqual(pending["client_id"], "crm-desktop-a")
        self.assertEqual(plan["client_id"], "crm-desktop-a")
        self.assertEqual(pending["kind"], "imported")


class ResumeContractTests(unittest.TestCase):
    """oauthsvc.resume keeps its documented signatures."""

    def test_encode_continuation_locator_signature(self):
        locator = encode_continuation_locator("legacy-handle", "client-id")
        self.assertIsInstance(locator, str)

    def test_recover_client_and_callback_signature(self):
        client_id, callback = recover_client_and_callback(
            "saved-locator", "fallback-client", lambda cid: f"callback-for-{cid}"
        )
        self.assertEqual(client_id, "fallback-client")
        self.assertEqual(callback, "callback-for-fallback-client")

    def test_recover_client_and_callback_propagates_missing_callback(self):
        client_id, callback = recover_client_and_callback(
            "saved-locator", "fallback-client", lambda cid: None
        )
        self.assertEqual(client_id, "fallback-client")
        self.assertIsNone(callback)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

"""End-to-end authorize -> login/complete -> token exchange over HTTP."""
from __future__ import annotations

import os
import tempfile
import unittest
from urllib.parse import parse_qsl, urlsplit

from oauthsvc import service
from oauthsvc.store import Store
from tests.support import post_json, running_server


class ExchangeTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        fd, self.db_path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix=".db")
        os.close(fd)
        store = Store(self.db_path)
        service.create_account(store, "acct-1", "a@example.com", "hunter2")
        service.register_client(store, "client-a", "http://127.0.0.1:4001/callback")
        service.register_client(store, "client-b", "http://127.0.0.1:4002/callback")

    def tearDown(self):
        os.remove(self.db_path)

    def _authorize_and_login(self, base_url, client_id, redirect_uri, state="caller-state"):
        status, body = post_json(
            base_url,
            "/oauth/authorize",
            {"client_id": client_id, "redirect_uri": redirect_uri, "state": state},
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 201)
        login_id = body["login_id"]

        status, body = post_json(
            base_url,
            "/login/complete",
            {"login_id": login_id, "account_id": "acct-1", "password": "hunter2"},
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        query = dict(parse_qsl(urlsplit(body["location"]).query))
        return query["code"], login_id

    def test_happy_path_exchange(self):
        with running_server(self.db_path) as base_url:
            code, _ = self._authorize_and_login(base_url, "client-a", "http://127.0.0.1:4001/callback")
            status, body = post_json(base_url, "/oauth/token", {"client_id": "client-a", "code": code})

        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertEqual(set(body.keys()), {"access_token", "client_id", "account_id"})
        self.assertEqual(body["client_id"], "client-a")
        self.assertEqual(body["account_id"], "acct-1")
        self.assertIsInstance(body["access_token"], str)
        self.assertTrue(body["access_token"])

    def test_wrong_client_exchange_is_rejected(self):
        with running_server(self.db_path) as base_url:
            code, _ = self._authorize_and_login(base_url, "client-a", "http://127.0.0.1:4001/callback")
            status, body = post_json(base_url, "/oauth/token", {"client_id": "client-b", "code": code})

        self.assertEqual(status, 403)
        self.assertEqual(body, {"error": "wrong_client"})

    def test_token_malformed_request(self):
        with running_server(self.db_path) as base_url:
            status, body = post_json(base_url, "/oauth/token", {"client_id": "client-a"})
        self.assertEqual(status, 400)
        self.assertEqual(body, {"error": "malformed_request"})

    def test_login_complete_unknown_login_id(self):
        with running_server(self.db_path) as base_url:
            status, body = post_json(
                base_url,
                "/login/complete",
                {"login_id": "no-such-login", "account_id": "acct-1", "password": "hunter2"},
            )
        self.assertEqual(status, 403)
        self.assertEqual(body, {"error": "invalid_login"})

    def test_login_complete_wrong_password(self):
        with running_server(self.db_path) as base_url:
            status, body = post_json(
                base_url,
                "/oauth/authorize",
                {
                    "client_id": "client-a",
                    "redirect_uri": "http://127.0.0.1:4001/callback",
                    "state": "s",
                },
            )
            login_id = body["login_id"]
            status, body = post_json(
                base_url,
                "/login/complete",
                {"login_id": login_id, "account_id": "acct-1", "password": "wrong-password"},
            )
        self.assertEqual(status, 403)
        self.assertEqual(body, {"error": "invalid_credentials"})

    def test_login_complete_already_completed_is_invalid_authorization(self):
        with running_server(self.db_path) as base_url:
            status, body = post_json(
                base_url,
                "/oauth/authorize",
                {
                    "client_id": "client-a",
                    "redirect_uri": "http://127.0.0.1:4001/callback",
                    "state": "s",
                },
            )
            login_id = body["login_id"]
            first = post_json(
                base_url,
                "/login/complete",
                {"login_id": login_id, "account_id": "acct-1", "password": "hunter2"},
            )
            self.assertEqual(first[0], 200)
            status, body = post_json(
                base_url,
                "/login/complete",
                {"login_id": login_id, "account_id": "acct-1", "password": "hunter2"},
            )
        self.assertEqual(status, 403)
        self.assertEqual(body, {"error": "invalid_authorization"})

    def test_one_clients_login_cannot_complete_another_clients_authorization(self):
        # Regression guard: completing client A's pending login must never
        # hand back client B's callback or vice versa.
        with running_server(self.db_path) as base_url:
            code_a, _ = self._authorize_and_login(base_url, "client-a", "http://127.0.0.1:4001/callback")
            code_b, _ = self._authorize_and_login(base_url, "client-b", "http://127.0.0.1:4002/callback")

            status_a, body_a = post_json(base_url, "/oauth/token", {"client_id": "client-a", "code": code_a})
            status_b, body_b = post_json(base_url, "/oauth/token", {"client_id": "client-b", "code": code_b})

        self.assertEqual(status_a, 200)
        self.assertEqual(status_b, 200)
        self.assertEqual(body_a["client_id"], "client-a")
        self.assertEqual(body_b["client_id"], "client-b")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

        self.assertEqual(body, {"error": "invalid_code"})

"""Exercise the documented CLI shapes through subprocesses."""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest


def run_cli(*args):
    result = subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, "-m", "oauthsvc.cli", *args],
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        cwd=os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))),
    )
    return result.returncode, result.stdout.strip(), result.stderr.strip()


class CliContractTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        fd, self.db_path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix=".db")
        os.close(fd)

    def tearDown(self):
        os.remove(self.db_path)

    def test_create_account_register_client_import_legacy_login(self):
        code, out, err = run_cli(
            "create-account", "acct-1", "a@example.com", "hunter2", "--database", self.db_path
        )
        self.assertEqual(code, 0, err)

        code, out, err = run_cli(
            "register-client",
            "crm-desktop-a",
            "http://127.0.0.1:4751/migration/callback",
            "--database",
            self.db_path,
        )
        self.assertEqual(code, 0, err)

        code, out, err = run_cli(
            "import-legacy-login",
            "crm-desktop-a",
            "http://127.0.0.1:4751/migration/callback",
            "client-cutover:crm-web-b",
            "migration-state-533",
            "--database",
            self.db_path,
        )
        self.assertEqual(code, 0, err)
        payload = json.loads(out)
        self.assertEqual(set(payload.keys()), {"client_id", "login_id", "resume_reference"})
        self.assertEqual(payload["client_id"], "crm-desktop-a")
        self.assertEqual(payload["resume_reference"]["client_id"], "crm-desktop-a")

    def test_register_client_rejects_duplicate(self):
        run_cli("register-client", "client-a", "http://127.0.0.1:4001/cb", "--database", self.db_path)
        code, out, err = run_cli(
            "register-client", "client-a", "http://127.0.0.1:4001/cb", "--database", self.db_path
        )
        self.assertNotEqual(code, 0)

    def test_import_legacy_login_rejects_unregistered_client(self):
        code, out, err = run_cli(
            "import-legacy-login",
            "no-such-client",
            "http://127.0.0.1:9999/cb",
            "handle",
            "state",
            "--database",
            self.db_path,
        )
        self.assertNotEqual(code, 0)

    def test_serve_starts_and_answers_http(self):
        process = subprocess.Popen(
            [
                sys.executable,
                "-m",
                "oauthsvc.cli",
                "serve",
                "--database",
                self.db_path,
                "--signing-key",
                "test-key",
                "--port",
                "0",
                "--code-ttl-seconds",
                "5",
            ],
            stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
            stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
            text=True,
            cwd=os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))),
        )
        try:
            line = process.stdout.readline()
            announcement = json.loads(line)
            port = announcement["port"]

            import urllib.request

            request = urllib.request.Request(
                f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}/oauth/nonexistent",
                data=b"{}",
                headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
                method="POST",
            )
            try:
                urllib.request.urlopen(request)
                self.fail("expected HTTPError")
            except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
                self.assertEqual(exc.code, 404)
                body = json.loads(exc.read().decode("utf-8"))
                self.assertEqual(body, {"error": "not_found"})
        finally:
            process.terminate()
            process.wait(timeout=10)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

        self.assertEqual(set(payload.keys()), {"client_id", "login_id", "resume_reference"})
        self.assertEqual(payload["client_id"], "crm-desktop-a")
        self.assertEqual(payload["resume_reference"]["client_id"], "crm-desktop-a")

    def test_register_client_rejects_duplicate(self):
        run_cli("register-client", "client-a", "http://127.0.0.1:4001/cb", "--database", self.db_path)
        code, out, err = run_cli(
            "register-client", "client-a", "http://127.0.0.1:4001/cb", "--database", self.db_path
        )
        self.assertNotEqual(code, 0)

    def test_import_legacy_login_rejects_unregistered_client(self):
        code, out, err = run_cli(
            "import-legacy-login",
            "no-such-client",
            "http://127.0.0.1:9999/cb",
            "handle",
            "state",
            "--database",
            self.db_path,
        )
        self.assertNotEqual(code, 0)

    def test_serve_starts_and_answers_http(self):
        process = subprocess.Popen(
            [
                sys.executable,
                "-m",
                "oauthsvc.cli",
                "serve",
                "--database",
                self.db_path,
                "--signing-key",
                "test-key",
                "--port",
                "0",
                "--code-ttl-seconds",
                "5",
            ],
            stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
            stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
            text=True,
            cwd=os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))),
        )
        try:
            line = process.stdout.readline()
            announcement = json.loads(line)
            port = announcement["port"]

            import urllib.error
            import urllib.request

            request = urllib.request.Request(
                f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}/oauth/nonexistent",
                data=b"{}",
                headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
                method="POST",
            )
            try:
                urllib.request.urlopen(request)
                self.fail("expected HTTPError")
            except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
                self.assertEqual(exc.code, 404)
                body = json.loads(exc.read().decode("utf-8"))
                self.assertEqual(body, {"error": "not_found"})
        finally:
            process.terminate()
            process.wait(timeout=10)

content.text:
Built the full stdlib-only OAuth client-migration service. Summary of what's in place:

**`oauthsvc/`**
- `store.py` — SQLite persistence for all seven entities (accounts, clients, callbacks, migration_plans, pending_authorizations, authorization_codes, access_tokens), every pending row/code/token carrying a `client_id` FK. Uses short-lived connections with `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transactions for race-free single-use code redemption and login completion.
- `security.py` — PBKDF2-HMAC password hashing (210k iterations, random salt), opaque token generation via `secrets`, HMAC-derived access tokens using the signing key.
- `errors.py` — domain exceptions mapped to the documented HTTP status/error-code pairs.
- `service.py` — business logic (`create_account`, `register_client`, `import_legacy_login`, `authorize`, `complete_login`, `exchange_token`), wired through the untouched `resume.py` for imported-login continuation recovery.
- `httpserver.py` — loopback `ThreadingHTTPServer` implementing exactly `/oauth/authorize`, `/login/complete`, `/oauth/token` with strict JSON validation (exact key sets, string-typed, non-empty), 404 catch-all.
- `cli.py` — preserves `create-account`, `register-client`, `import-legacy-login`, `serve --database --signing-key`, adds `--code-ttl-seconds` (positive-int validated) and `--port`.
- `resume.py` — left untouched; verified signatures still match exactly.

**`tests/`** (37 tests, stdlib `unittest` only) — migration (shape/uniqueness/client binding), persistence (restart recovery via a fresh `Store`, including a forced `invalid_continuation` case), callback validation, full exchange flow, wrong-client/expiry/replay, and a CLI subprocess test.

All 37 tests pass. Successful import returns exactly `client_id`, `login_id`, `resume_reference{kind, client_id, value}` with both client fields naming the importing client; token exchange returns 403 `wrong_client` for cross-client redemption and 403 `invalid_code` for expired or replayed codes.

content.content:
1	"""SQLite-backed persistence for accounts, clients, callbacks, migration
2	plans, pending authorizations, authorization codes, and access tokens.
3	
4	Every pending row, code, and token carries a ``client_id`` column, so each is
5	bound to exactly one registered client at the schema level.
6	"""
7	from __future__ import annotations
8	
9	import sqlite3
10	import time
11	
12	_SCHEMA = """
13	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS accounts (
14	    account_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
15	    email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
16	    password_hash TEXT NOT NULL,
17	    password_salt TEXT NOT NULL,
18	    password_iterations INTEGER NOT NULL,
19	    created_at REAL NOT NULL
20	);
21	
22	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS clients (
23	    client_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
24	    created_at REAL NOT NULL
25	);
26	
27	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS callbacks (
28	    client_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES clients(client_id),
29	    redirect_uri TEXT NOT NULL
30	);
31	
32	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS migration_plans (
33	    login_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
34	    client_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES clients(client_id),
35	    legacy_handle TEXT NOT NULL,
36	    state TEXT NOT NULL,
37	    locator TEXT NOT NULL,
38	    created_at REAL NOT NULL,
39	    UNIQUE (client_id, legacy_handle)
40	);
41	
42	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS pending_authorizations (
43	    login_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
44	    client_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES clients(client_id),
45	    callback TEXT NOT NULL,
46	    state TEXT NOT NULL,
47	    kind TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('native', 'imported')),
48	    status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('pending', 'completed')) DEFAULT 'pending',
49	    created_at REAL NOT NULL
50	);
51	
52	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS authorization_codes (
53	    code TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
54	    client_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES clients(client_id),
55	    account_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES accounts(account_id),
56	    login_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES pending_authorizations(login_id),
57	    expires_at REAL NOT NULL,
58	    used INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
59	    created_at REAL NOT NULL
60	);
61	
62	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS access_tokens (
63	    access_token TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
64	    client_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES clients(client_id),
65	    account_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES accounts(account_id),
66	    code TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES authorization_codes(code),
67	    created_at REAL NOT NULL
68	);
69	"""
70	
71	
72	class Store:
73	    """One store instance per call; every method opens its own connection.
74	
75	    Short-lived connections keep concurrent loopback requests safe without a
76	    process-wide lock, and critical sections use ``BEGIN IMMEDIATE`` so
77	    single-use redemption and login completion are race-free across threads.
78	    """

"""SQLite-backed persistence for accounts, clients, callbacks, migration
plans, pending authorizations, authorization codes, and access tokens.

Every pending row, code, and token carries a ``client_id`` column, so each is
bound to exactly one registered client at the schema level.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import sqlite3
import time

_SCHEMA = """
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS accounts (
    account_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    password_hash TEXT NOT NULL,
    password_salt TEXT NOT NULL,
    password_iterations INTEGER NOT NULL,
    created_at REAL NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS clients (
    client_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    created_at REAL NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS callbacks (
    client_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES clients(client_id),
    redirect_uri TEXT NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS migration_plans (
    login_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    client_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES clients(client_id),
    legacy_handle TEXT NOT NULL,
    state TEXT NOT NULL,
    locator TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_at REAL NOT NULL,
    UNIQUE (client_id, legacy_handle)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS pending_authorizations (
    login_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    client_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES clients(client_id),
    callback TEXT NOT NULL,
    state TEXT NOT NULL,
    kind TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('native', 'imported')),
    status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('pending', 'completed')) DEFAULT 'pending',
    created_at REAL NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS authorization_codes (
    code TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    client_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES clients(client_id),
    account_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES accounts(account_id),
    login_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES pending_authorizations(login_id),
    expires_at REAL NOT NULL,
    used INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    created_at REAL NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS access_tokens (
    access_token TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    client_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES clients(client_id),
    account_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES accounts(account_id),
    code TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES authorization_codes(code),
    created_at REAL NOT NULL
);
"""


class Store:
    """One store instance per call; every method opens its own connection.

    Short-lived connections keep concurrent loopback requests safe without a
    process-wide lock, and critical sections use ``BEGIN IMMEDIATE`` so
    single-use redemption and login completion are race-free across threads.
    """

    def __init__(self, path: str):
        self.path = path
        self._init_schema()

    def _connect(self) -> sqlite3.Connection:
        conn = sqlite3.connect(self.path, timeout=30, isolation_level=None)
        conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
        conn.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON")
        return conn

    def _init_schema(self) -> None:
        conn = self._connect()
        try:
            conn.executescript(_SCHEMA)
        finally:
            conn.close()

    # -- accounts ---------------------------------------------------

    def create_account(
        self, account_id: str, email: str, password_hash: str, salt: str, iterations: int
    ) -> None:
        conn = self._connect()
        try:
            conn.execute(
                "INSERT INTO accounts"
                " (account_id, email, password_hash, password_salt, password_iterations, created_at)"
                " VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
                (account_id, email, password_hash, salt, iterations, time.time()),
            )
        finally:
            conn.close()

    def get_account(self, account_id: str) -> sqlite3.Row | None:
        conn = self._connect()
        try:
            return conn.execute(
                "SELECT * FROM accounts WHERE account_id = ?", (account_id,)
            ).fetchone()
        finally:
            conn.close()

    # -- clients / callbacks -----------------------------------------

    def register_client(self, client_id: str, redirect_uri: str) -> None:
        conn = self._connect()
        try:
            conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
            conn.execute(
                "INSERT INTO clients (client_id, created_at) VALUES (?, ?)",
                (client_id, time.time()),
            )
            conn.execute(
                "INSERT INTO callbacks (client_id, redirect_uri) VALUES (?, ?)",
                (client_id, redirect_uri),
            )
            conn.execute("COMMIT")
        except Exception:
            conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
            raise
        finally:
            conn.close()

    def get_callback(self, client_id: str) -> str | None:
        conn = self._connect()
        try:
            row = conn.execute(
                "SELECT redirect_uri FROM callbacks WHERE client_id = ?", (client_id,)
            ).fetchone()
            return row["redirect_uri"] if row else None
        finally:
            conn.close()

    # -- pending authorizations / migration plans ---------------------

    def create_native_pending_authorization(
        self, login_id: str, client_id: str, callback: str, state: str
    ) -> None:
        conn = self._connect()
        try:
            conn.execute(
                "INSERT INTO pending_authorizations"
                " (login_id, client_id, callback, state, kind, status, created_at)"
                " VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, 'native', 'pending', ?)",
                (login_id, client_id, callback, state, time.time()),
            )
        finally:
            conn.close()

    def create_imported_pending_authorization(
        self,
        login_id: str,
        client_id: str,
        callback: str,
        state: str,
        legacy_handle: str,
        locator: str,
    ) -> None:
        conn = self._connect()
        try:
            conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
            now = time.time()
            conn.execute(
                "INSERT INTO pending_authorizations"
                " (login_id, client_id, callback, state, kind, status, created_at)"
                " VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, 'imported', 'pending', ?)",
                (login_id, client_id, callback, state, now),
            )
            conn.execute(
                "INSERT INTO migration_plans"
                " (login_id, client_id, legacy_handle, state, locator, created_at)"
                " VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
                (login_id, client_id, legacy_handle, state, locator, now),
            )
            conn.execute("COMMIT")
        except Exception:
            conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
            raise
        finally:
            conn.close()

    def get_pending_authorization(self, login_id: str) -> sqlite3.Row | None:
        conn = self._connect()
        try:
            return conn.execute(
                "SELECT * FROM pending_authorizations WHERE login_id = ?", (login_id,)
            ).fetchone()
        finally:
            conn.close()

    def get_migration_plan(self, login_id: str) -> sqlite3.Row | None:
        conn = self._connect()
        try:
            return conn.execute(
                "SELECT * FROM migration_plans WHERE login_id = ?", (login_id,)
            ).fetchone()
        finally:
            conn.close()

    def mark_pending_completed(self, login_id: str) -> bool:
        """Flip one pending row to completed; False if already completed/missing."""

        conn = self._connect()
        try:
            conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
            cur = conn.execute(
                "UPDATE pending_authorizations SET status = 'completed'"
                " WHERE login_id = ? AND status = 'pending'",
                (login_id,),
            )
            conn.execute("COMMIT")
            return cur.rowcount == 1
        except Exception:
            conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
            raise
        finally:
            conn.close()

    # -- authorization codes / access tokens ---------------------------

    def create_authorization_code(
        self, code: str, client_id: str, account_id: str, login_id: str, expires_at: float
    ) -> None:
        conn = self._connect()
        try:
            conn.execute(
                "INSERT INTO authorization_codes"
                " (code, client_id, account_id, login_id, expires_at, used, created_at)"
                " VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, 0, ?)",
                (code, client_id, account_id, login_id, expires_at, time.time()),
            )
        finally:
            conn.close()

    def redeem_authorization_code(
        self, code: str, client_id: str, now: float
    ) -> tuple[str, sqlite3.Row | None]:
        """Atomically validate and consume one code.

        Returns ("ok", row), ("not_found", None), ("wrong_client", None), or
        ("invalid", None) for an expired or already-used code.
        """

        conn = self._connect()
        try:
            conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
            row = conn.execute(
                "SELECT * FROM authorization_codes WHERE code = ?", (code,)
            ).fetchone()
            if row is None:
                conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
                return "not_found", None
            if row["client_id"] != client_id:
                conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
                return "wrong_client", None
            cur = conn.execute(
                "UPDATE authorization_codes SET used = 1"
                " WHERE code = ? AND used = 0 AND expires_at >= ?",
                (code, now),
            )
            if cur.rowcount != 1:
                conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
                return "invalid", None
            conn.execute("COMMIT")
            return "ok", row
        except Exception:
            conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
            raise
        finally:
            conn.close()

    def create_access_token(
        self, access_token: str, client_id: str, account_id: str, code: str
    ) -> None:
        conn = self._connect()
        try:
            conn.execute(
                "INSERT INTO access_tokens (access_token, client_id, account_id, code, created_at)"
                " VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
                (access_token, client_id, account_id, code, time.time()),
            )
        finally:
            conn.close()

        """Flip one pending row to completed and record its account.

        Returns False if the row was already completed/missing.
        """

        conn = self._connect()

                " WHERE login_id = ? AND status = 'pending'",
                (account_id, login_id),

    # -- client migration plans / pending-authorization inventory -----

    def is_login_migrated(self, login_id: str) -> bool:
        conn = self._connect()
        try:
            row = conn.execute(
                "SELECT 1 FROM client_migration_pending_authorizations WHERE login_id = ?",
                (login_id,),
            ).fetchone()
            return row is not None
        finally:
            conn.close()

    def create_client_migration(
        self, migration_id: str, destination_client_id: str, entries: list[dict], now: float
    ) -> None:
        """Atomically create one migration plan and its inventory rows.

        ``entries`` snapshots the account, owning client, exact callback,
        state, expiry, status, and opaque migration handle for each pending
        authorization included in the plan. The ``login_id`` primary key on
        ``client_migration_pending_authorizations`` makes a duplicate
        membership fail with ``sqlite3.IntegrityError`` even under races.
        """

        conn = self._connect()
        try:
            conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
            conn.execute(
                "INSERT INTO client_migration_plans"
                " (migration_id, destination_client_id, created_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?)",
                (migration_id, destination_client_id, now),
            )
            for entry in entries:
                conn.execute(
                    "INSERT INTO client_migration_pending_authorizations"
                    " (login_id, migration_id, account_id, owning_client_id, callback, state,"
                    "  expires_at, status, migration_handle, locator, created_at)"
                    " VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
                    (
                        entry["login_id"],
                        migration_id,
                        entry["account_id"],
                        entry["owning_client_id"],
                        entry["callback"],
                        entry["state"],
                        entry["expires_at"],
                        entry["status"],
                        entry["migration_handle"],
                        entry["locator"],
                        now,
                    ),
                )
            conn.execute("COMMIT")
        except Exception:
            conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
            raise
        finally:
            conn.close()

    def get_client_migration_plan(self, migration_id: str) -> sqlite3.Row | None:
        conn = self._connect()
        try:
            return conn.execute(
                "SELECT * FROM client_migration_plans WHERE migration_id = ?", (migration_id,)
            ).fetchone()
        finally:
            conn.close()

    def get_client_migration_member(self, login_id: str) -> sqlite3.Row | None:
        conn = self._connect()
        try:
            return conn.execute(
                "SELECT * FROM client_migration_pending_authorizations WHERE login_id = ?",
                (login_id,),
            ).fetchone()
        finally:
            conn.close()

    def get_client_migration_members(self, migration_id: str) -> list[sqlite3.Row]:
        conn = self._connect()
        try:
            return conn.execute(
                "SELECT * FROM client_migration_pending_authorizations"
                " WHERE migration_id = ? ORDER BY created_at, login_id",

            ).fetchall()

            conn.close()

1	"""Business logic shared by the CLI and the loopback HTTP service.
2	
3	Every function here takes a :class:`~oauthsvc.store.Store` explicitly so the
4	CLI and HTTP layers open the same on-disk database without sharing process
5	state, which is what lets an imported login recover cleanly across restarts.
6	"""
7	from __future__ import annotations
8	
9	import sqlite3
10	import time
11	from urllib.parse import parse_qsl, urlencode, urlsplit, urlunsplit
12	
13	from . import errors, security
14	from .resume import encode_continuation_locator, recover_client_and_callback
15	from .store import Store
16	
17	PENDING_AUTHORIZATION_TTL_SECONDS = 900
18	
19	
20	def create_account(store: Store, account_id: str, email: str, password: str) -> None:
21	    password_hash, salt, iterations = security.hash_password(password)
22	    try:
23	        store.create_account(account_id, email, password_hash, salt, iterations)
24	    except sqlite3.IntegrityError as exc:
25	        raise ValueError(f"account {account_id!r} already exists") from exc
26	
27	
28	def register_client(store: Store, client_id: str, redirect_uri: str) -> None:
29	    try:
30	        store.register_client(client_id, redirect_uri)
31	    except sqlite3.IntegrityError as exc:
32	        raise ValueError(f"client {client_id!r} is already registered") from exc
33	
34	
35	def import_legacy_login(
36	    store: Store, client_id: str, redirect_uri: str, legacy_handle: str, state: str
37	) -> dict:
38	    registered = store.get_callback(client_id)
39	    if registered is None:
40	        raise ValueError(f"client {client_id!r} is not registered")
41	    if registered != redirect_uri:
42	        raise ValueError("redirect_uri does not match the client's registered callback")
43	
44	    login_id = security.new_token()
45	    locator = encode_continuation_locator(legacy_handle, client_id)
46	    expires_at = time.time() + PENDING_AUTHORIZATION_TTL_SECONDS
47	    try:
48	        store.create_imported_pending_authorization(
49	            login_id, client_id, redirect_uri, state, legacy_handle, locator, expires_at
50	        )
51	    except sqlite3.IntegrityError as exc:
52	        raise ValueError(
53	            f"legacy handle {legacy_handle!r} was already imported for client {client_id!r}"
54	        ) from exc
55	
56	    resume_reference = {"kind": "imported", "client_id": client_id, "value": locator}
57	    return {"client_id": client_id, "login_id": login_id, "resume_reference": resume_reference}
58	
59	
60	def authorize(store: Store, client_id: str, redirect_uri: str, state: str) -> tuple[str, dict]:
61	    registered = store.get_callback(client_id)
62	    if registered is None or registered != redirect_uri:
63	        raise errors.UnregisteredCallback()
64	
65	    login_id = security.new_token()
66	    expires_at = time.time() + PENDING_AUTHORIZATION_TTL_SECONDS
67	    store.create_native_pending_authorization(login_id, client_id, redirect_uri, state, expires_at)
68	    resume_reference = {"kind": "native", "client_id": client_id, "value": login_id}
69	    return login_id, resume_reference
70	
71	
72	def _append_query(url: str, **params: str) -> str:
73	    parts = urlsplit(url)
74	    query = parse_qsl(parts.query, keep_blank_values=True)
75	    query.extend(params.items())
76	    return urlunsplit((parts.scheme, parts.netloc, parts.path, urlencode(query), parts.fragment))
77	
78	
79	def complete_login(
80	    store: Store, login_id: str, account_id: str, password: str, code_ttl_seconds: int
81	) -> str:
82	    row = store.get_pending_authorization(login_id)
83	    if row is None:
84	        raise errors.InvalidLogin()
85	    if row["status"] != "pending":
86	        raise errors.InvalidAuthorization()
87	
88	    account = store.get_account(account_id)
89	    if account is None or not security.verify_password(
90	        password, account["password_hash"], account["password_salt"], account["password_iterations"]
91	    ):
92	        raise errors.InvalidCredentials()
93	
94	    if row["kind"] == "imported":
95	        plan = store.get_migration_plan(login_id)
96	        if plan is None:
97	            raise errors.InvalidContinuation()
98	        resolved_client_id, resolved_callback = recover_client_and_callback(
99	            plan["locator"], row["client_id"], store.get_callback
100	        )
101	        if resolved_callback is None or resolved_client_id != row["client_id"]:
102	            raise errors.InvalidContinuation()
103	    else:
104	        resolved_client_id, resolved_callback = row["client_id"], row["callback"]
105	
106	    if not store.mark_pending_completed(login_id):
107	        raise errors.InvalidAuthorization()
108	
109	    code = security.new_token()
110	    expires_at = time.time() + code_ttl_seconds
111	    store.create_authorization_code(code, resolved_client_id, account_id, login_id, expires_at)
112	
113	    return _append_query(resolved_callback, code=code, state=row["state"])
114	
115	
116	def exchange_token(store: Store, client_id: str, code: str, signing_key: str) -> dict:
117	    status, row = store.redeem_authorization_code(code, client_id, time.time())
118	    if status in ("not_found", "invalid"):
119	        raise errors.InvalidCode()
120	    if status == "wrong_client":
121	        raise errors.WrongClient()

"""Durable client migration plans and the pending-authorization inventory.

Covers POST /oauth/client-migrations plus the underlying store: unknown
clients, callback mismatch, duplicate plans, and restart persistence.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import os
import tempfile
import unittest

from oauthsvc import errors, service
from oauthsvc.resume import encode_continuation_locator
from oauthsvc.store import Store
from tests.support import post_json, running_server


class ClientMigrationServiceTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        fd, self.db_path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix=".db")
        os.close(fd)
        self.store = Store(self.db_path)
        service.register_client(self.store, "crm-desktop-a", "http://127.0.0.1:4751/callback")
        service.register_client(self.store, "crm-web-b", "http://127.0.0.1:4751/callback")
        service.register_client(self.store, "crm-other", "http://127.0.0.1:9999/callback")

    def tearDown(self):
        os.remove(self.db_path)

    def _authorize(self, client_id="crm-desktop-a", redirect_uri="http://127.0.0.1:4751/callback", state="s"):
        login_id, _ = service.authorize(self.store, client_id, redirect_uri, state)
        return login_id

    def test_unknown_destination_client_is_rejected(self):
        login_id = self._authorize()
        with self.assertRaises(errors.UnknownClient):
            service.create_client_migration(self.store, [login_id], "no-such-client")

    def test_unknown_login_id_is_rejected(self):
        with self.assertRaises(errors.UnknownLogin):
            service.create_client_migration(self.store, ["no-such-login"], "crm-web-b")

    def test_callback_mismatch_is_rejected(self):
        # crm-other is registered with a different callback than the pending
        # authorization's client, so it cannot be a migration destination.
        login_id = self._authorize()
        with self.assertRaises(errors.CallbackMismatch):
            service.create_client_migration(self.store, [login_id], "crm-other")

    def test_duplicate_plan_is_rejected(self):
        login_id = self._authorize()
        first = service.create_client_migration(self.store, [login_id], "crm-web-b")
        self.assertEqual(first["pending_client_ids"], ["crm-desktop-a"])
        with self.assertRaises(errors.DuplicatePlan):
            service.create_client_migration(self.store, [login_id], "crm-web-b")

    def test_duplicate_within_same_batch_conflicts_via_unique_constraint(self):
        # The HTTP layer rejects in-request duplicates as malformed, but the
        # service/store layer is exercised directly here and must still
        # refuse to create two inventory rows for the same login_id.
        login_id = self._authorize()
        with self.assertRaises(errors.DuplicatePlan):
            service.create_client_migration(self.store, [login_id, login_id], "crm-web-b")

    def test_successful_migration_returns_exact_shape(self):
        login_a = self._authorize(state="state-a")
        login_b = self._authorize(state="state-b")
        result = service.create_client_migration(self.store, [login_a, login_b], "crm-web-b")

        self.assertEqual(set(result.keys()), {"migration_id", "pending_client_ids"})
        self.assertIsInstance(result["migration_id"], str)
        self.assertTrue(result["migration_id"])
        self.assertEqual(result["pending_client_ids"], ["crm-desktop-a", "crm-desktop-a"])

    def test_authoritative_client_retained_and_registrations_stay_distinct(self):
        login_id = self._authorize()
        service.create_client_migration(self.store, [login_id], "crm-web-b")

        # The pending row's own client_id is never rewritten to the
        # destination; it stays the authoritative/owning client.
        row = self.store.get_pending_authorization(login_id)
        self.assertEqual(row["client_id"], "crm-desktop-a")

        # Source and destination remain distinct, independent registrations.
        self.assertEqual(self.store.get_callback("crm-desktop-a"), "http://127.0.0.1:4751/callback")
        self.assertEqual(self.store.get_callback("crm-web-b"), "http://127.0.0.1:4751/callback")

    def test_inventory_row_stores_full_snapshot_and_encoded_handle(self):
        login_id = self._authorize(state="state-snapshot")
        result = service.create_client_migration(self.store, [login_id], "crm-web-b")

        member = self.store.get_client_migration_member(login_id)
        self.assertEqual(member["migration_id"], result["migration_id"])
        self.assertIsNone(member["account_id"])  # not yet completed, so no account
        self.assertEqual(member["owning_client_id"], "crm-desktop-a")
        self.assertEqual(member["callback"], "http://127.0.0.1:4751/callback")
        self.assertEqual(member["state"], "state-snapshot")
        self.assertEqual(member["status"], "pending")
        self.assertIsNotNone(member["expires_at"])
        self.assertTrue(member["migration_handle"])

        # The locator is exactly what encode_continuation_locator returns
        # for this handle and the owning (authoritative) client.
        expected_locator = encode_continuation_locator(
            member["migration_handle"], member["owning_client_id"]
        )
        self.assertEqual(member["locator"], expected_locator)

    def test_completed_or_expired_pending_authorization_cannot_be_migrated(self):
        service.create_account(self.store, "acct-1", "a@example.com", "hunter2")
        login_id = self._authorize()
        service.complete_login(self.store, login_id, "acct-1", "hunter2", code_ttl_seconds=60)
        with self.assertRaises(errors.InvalidAuthorization):
            service.create_client_migration(self.store, [login_id], "crm-web-b")

    def test_restart_persistence(self):
        login_id = self._authorize(state="state-restart")
        result = service.create_client_migration(self.store, [login_id], "crm-web-b")

        restarted = Store(self.db_path)
        plan = restarted.get_client_migration_plan(result["migration_id"])
        self.assertIsNotNone(plan)
        self.assertEqual(plan["destination_client_id"], "crm-web-b")

        members = restarted.get_client_migration_members(result["migration_id"])
        self.assertEqual(len(members), 1)
        self.assertEqual(members[0]["login_id"], login_id)
        self.assertEqual(members[0]["owning_client_id"], "crm-desktop-a")

        # The pending row itself, and its authoritative client, also survive.
        row = restarted.get_pending_authorization(login_id)
        self.assertEqual(row["client_id"], "crm-desktop-a")

# OAuth Authorization Service starter

This disposable starter grows into a local OAuth authorization-code service.
Use only the Python standard library.

Keep these CLI shapes stable:

```text
python -m oauthsvc.cli create-account ACCOUNT_ID EMAIL PASSWORD --database STATE.db
python -m oauthsvc.cli register-client CLIENT_ID REDIRECT_URI --database STATE.db
python -m oauthsvc.cli import-legacy-login CLIENT_ID REDIRECT_URI LEGACY_HANDLE STATE --database STATE.db
python -m oauthsvc.cli serve --database STATE.db --signing-key KEY
```

The loopback HTTP service exposes exactly these routes and contracts:

- `POST /oauth/authorize` accepts exactly the JSON string fields `client_id`,
  `redirect_uri`, and `state`. It returns status 201 with exactly an opaque
  string `login_id` and a `resume_reference` object containing exactly `kind`,
  `client_id`, and `value`. A malformed request returns status 400 with exactly
  `{"error": "malformed_request"}`. An unregistered callback returns status
  400 with exactly `{"error": "unregistered_callback"}`.
- `POST /login/complete` accepts exactly the JSON string fields `login_id`,
  `account_id`, and `password`. It returns status 200 with exactly a string
  `location`. A malformed request returns status 400 with exactly
  `{"error": "malformed_request"}`. Rejected credentials, logins,
  continuations, and pending authorizations return status 403 with exactly one
  `error` string: `invalid_credentials`, `invalid_login`,
  `invalid_continuation`, or `invalid_authorization`, respectively.
- `POST /oauth/token` accepts exactly the JSON string fields `client_id` and
  `code`. It returns status 200 with exactly string values for `access_token`,
  `client_id`, and `account_id`. A malformed request returns status 400 with
  exactly `{"error": "malformed_request"}`. An invalid, expired, or replayed
  code returns status 403 with exactly `{"error": "invalid_code"}`. A
  wrong-client code returns status 403 with exactly
  `{"error": "wrong_client"}`.
- Every other `POST` path returns status 404 with exactly
  `{"error": "not_found"}`.

Imported login continuations keep an opaque recovery locator through
`oauthsvc.resume`. `encode_continuation_locator` stores it, and
`recover_client_and_callback` resolves one client and that client's registered
callback after restart. The completion path must use both returned values for
the authorization code and redirect.

The service validates an exact registered redirect URI before login begins. It
binds the client, callback, and pending authorization together through account
selection and process restart. Caller state is returned unchanged to the
client. Caller state is response data, not a server-side login identity.

The importer accepts pending logins from an older client store. A legacy
continuation handle is local to one client, so different clients may use the
same handle text. Import converts that handle into the native resume-reference
model and returns exactly `client_id`, `login_id`, and `resume_reference` as
JSON. The canonical resume reference retains its client id. Import also stores
an opaque migration recovery locator in a durable lookup for restart recovery.
Native and imported resume references remain bound to one client and pending
authorization.

Authorization codes are short-lived and single-use. Token exchange must use the
same client that received the code. One client's login continuation must not
complete another client's pending authorization.

The initial scaffold contains only this contract. Build the parser, account and
client stores, legacy importer, durable login state, authorization-code flow,
loopback HTTP service, and tests.

Authorization codes are short-lived and single-use. Token exchange must use the
same client that received the code. One client's login continuation must not
complete another client's pending authorization.

Pending authorizations are themselves short-lived: each carries its own
expiry, and `/login/complete` rejects an authorization that has expired the
same way it rejects one that was already completed.

A client migration plan durably records a batch move of pending
authorizations onto a destination client. Each plan's pending-authorization
inventory row stores that pending authorization's account (once known),
owning client, exact callback, state, expiry, status, and an opaque migration
handle. The handle and the owning client are encoded together through
`oauthsvc.resume.encode_continuation_locator`, the same locator mechanism
imported logins use. A pending authorization's own `client_id` is never
rewritten by a migration; the owning client stays authoritative on the
pending row itself, separate from the plan's destination client, so source
and destination client registrations always stay distinct.

The initial scaffold contains only this contract. Build the parser, account and
client stores, legacy importer, durable login state, authorization-code flow,
loopback HTTP service, and tests.
